outline.chapter_title: Foundations of Reinforcement Learning for Language Models
outline.description: This chapter establishes the necessary background knowledge, defining the notation for autoregressive policies, rewards, and queries. It reviews existing algorithms like Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), highlighting their mechanics, specifically focusing on token-level importance sampling and the reliance on value models or group-relative advantages.
subtopics: Mathematical Notation: Policies, Queries, Responses, and Likelihoods
Reward Modeling and Verification in LLMs
Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO): Objectives and Value Model Dependencies
Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO): Eliminating the Value Model via Group Advantages
Token-Level Importance Ratios in Current State-of-the-Art Algorithms

outline.chapter_title: The Stability Crisis: Diagnosing Failures in Token-Level Optimization
outline.description: Here we analyze why current methods fail when scaling to massive models and long contexts. We dissect the theoretical flaw in GRPO regarding the misapplication of importance sampling at the token level versus the sequence level. This chapter explains how high-variance noise accumulates over time steps, leading to catastrophic model collapse, particularly in Mixture-of-Experts architectures.
subtopics: The Off-Policy Challenge in Large Batch Training
Theoretical Flaw: Single-Sample Estimation vs. Expectation Correction
Catastrophic Collapse: Irreversibility and Hyperparameter Sensitivity
Specific Instabilities in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Models: Expert Activation Volatility

outline.description: This core chapter details the proposed GSPO algorithm. It derives the new objective function based on sequence-level likelihood rather than token-level probability. Students will learn how GSPO aligns the unit of optimization with the unit of reward, implements length-normalized importance ratios, and applies clipping at the sequence level to filter out-poly samples effectively.
subtopics: Core Principle: Aligning Optimization Units with Reward Units
Length Normalization: Controlling Variance Across Different Response Lengths

outline.chapter_title: Mathematical Analysis: Gradient Dynamics and Variants
outline.description: (Advanced Topic) A rigorous mathematical breakdown comparing the gradient flows of GRPO and GSPO. This chapter proves mathematically why GSPO produces more stable gradients by weighting tokens equally within a sequence. It also introduces 'GSPO-token,' a hybrid variant designed for scenarios requiring fine-grained, token-specific advantage adjustments without sacrificing stability.
